pages.sections — actual persisted values for tool pages created via each of the two paths

code_requests.why: Find how page-build-handler (or whichever action processes needs_content_page items) reads pages.sections to derive buildable work, and whether it recognizes 'hero-tool', 'tool-guide-intro', 'tool-cta' as writable slots or only a fixed vocabulary that excludes them.

data_requests.sql: SELECT p.id, p.name, p.page_type, p.sections, p.build_status FROM pages p WHERE p.site_id = (SELECT id FROM sites WHERE domain = 'robot-hands.com') AND p.page_type = 'tool'
data_requests.why: Shows the actual declared sections on live tool pages for this site — settles whether create_tool_component_action.go's omission of the sections column produced an empty array, null, or something else, and whether deploy_tool_action.go's 4-section array is what's actually stored.

data_requests.sql: SELECT id, item_type, status, item_key, result, error, created_at FROM site_work_items WHERE item_key LIKE 'tool_content:%' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20
data_requests.why: Shows whether tool_content work items actually resolve to needs_human_review with identical wording, which is the runtime behavior the hypothesis claims but which no log line in this bundle currently demonstrates.

revised_hypothesis: The two emitters are not siblings behaving identically. deploy_tool_action.go explicitly declares FOUR sections for the tool page — hero-tool, tool-guide-intro, the tool widget itself, and tool-cta — which already correspond to exactly the hero/guide/CTA shape that content_guidance asks a handler to write. That contradicts the premise that 'the platform-wide finished shape of a tool page is the single widget slot': at least this emitter's pages are NOT single-slot. create_tool_component_action.go's pages INSERT, by contrast, never mentions the sections column at all — it neither declares the single slot nor an empty array; the value is whatever the column default is, which is not shown anywhere in this bundle. So the claim that both emitters raise a needs_content_page item against a page whose declared sections cannot satisfy it is unverified for one emitter and actively contradicted for the other. If page-build-handler really derives buildable work purely from pages.sections, the deploy_tool_action.go path (hero-tool/tool-guide-intro/tool-cta already declared) should be actionable, not a no-op — so the no-op, if it occurs, is more likely isolated to (or at least differs between) the create_tool_component_action.go path and whatever page-build-handler actually does with those specific section names, not a uniform platform-wide mismatch.
